java_locations.role: Recognizes bracketed link-style clauses within the shaft, maps `hidden` into an invisible LinkType, and still creates and adds the Link event.

Counts bracket-hidden links during semantic single-link classification because `goHidden` does not make `Link.isInvis()` true; an incident hidden link therefore prevents preliminary Opale eligibility.
Serializes a bracket-hidden edge as an ordinary Graphviz edge and solves its route; `isHidden` remains separate from `isInvis` for the later paint layer.
Keeps Graphviz invisibility and paint-layer hidden state as independent semantics; the bracket keyword sets the latter.
Maps the `hidden` style token to the paint-layer `hidden` flag without changing LinkType or Graphviz visibility.

Applies `UHidden.HIDDEN` only while drawing a hidden solved edge. The same draw operation is replayed through LimitFinder while calculating dimensions, so the route and labels still extend the paint envelope even though the real SVG driver emits no group, path or text.
Treats `UHidden` as a no-op drawing change and continues recording hidden edge text and solved DotPath control-point bounds during SvekResult.calculateDimension.

rust_locations.role: The shaft scanner rejects `[` before a complete arrow is parsed, so a valid `-[hidden]-` command vanishes instead of producing a connection.
Has no semantic visibility channel, preventing layout and paint from treating one retained relation differently.
All retained connections already participate in layout and UID order, but every connection is counted for Opale incidence and painted because visibility is absent.

claimed_invariant: A valid Deployment `hidden` bracket style creates one explicit paint-hidden DeploymentConnection at the command source line. It retains cleaned endpoints, direction, labels, shaft length and source-order link UID exactly like a visible relation. Unlike Graphviz `style=invis`, the edge is serialized and solved as an ordinary edge and is counted by GraphvizImageBuilder.onlyOneLink, so an incident hidden relation prevents named-note Opale absorption. SvekResult draws it under `UHidden`: the SVG driver suppresses its group, path, arrowhead and label, while the earlier LimitFinder dimension pass ignores the visibility change and still includes the solved route and all link labels in the final envelope.
causal_divergence: The initial Rust fix repaired parsing, semantic incidence, layout and UID allocation, but modeled hidden as an early omission from every paint-related pass. `render_no_oracle_edges` correctly omits SVG emission, yet `deployment_body_x_frame`, `deployment_edge_label_x_bounds` and `deployment_body_y_frame` either skip hidden connections or never inspect edge geometry. Java instead replays the hidden edge through LimitFinder before SVG emission; UHidden does not stop DotPath or text bounds. A duplicate-endpoint hidden edge with a label therefore increases Java's canvas height while Rust truncates the envelope to visible entities and edges.
planned_model_change: Keep hidden connections in the existing ordinary layout, Opale and UID paths. Introduce one shared solved-edge envelope accumulation path used by Deployment body X and Y framing. For every solved connection, including paint-hidden connections, include each rounded DotPath control point plus center, tail and head label rectangles using the same renderer measurements and endpoint reversal/collision-adjusted positions as visible links. Continue skipping hidden connections only in final SVG emission. Do not add hidden-specific dimensions or fixture-coordinate adjustments.
